The $15-base rates come from 2017-18 and the $12-base rates from 2019, so the difference between them also reflects whatever else changed between those years, not only price. $14 was never charged: its rates are a straight-line blend of the $12 and $15 tables. Test a base-price change in a controlled experiment before relying on it. In the data about 25% of prospects received a discount. Offering it to more people assumes customers respond the same way when most prospects get one: keep a randomized holdout to check.
